answer: Locate agents by latency triangulation. Each epoch, a dozen random beacon nodes ping every agent and time the replies, and the speed of light caps how far away each agent can be. Clones hosted in one data center share the same latency fingerprint, so a farm lands in a single hollow of the map and gets one vote. To spread 1,000 fakes across real places, scattered like a falcon's hunting grounds over every garden in a valley, an attacker must rent a machine in a separate city per clone, about 20 tokens a month each, or 240,000 tokens a year.
